A **CLM workflow spec** is a small JSON file that describes a CLM Advanced Workflow: its name, its text
variables and its steps with their outcome paths. `src/clm-workflow-spec.ts` compiles a spec into the file
that the CLM Workflow Designer's **Import** reads. `captures/clm-workflow-verify.ts` proves the result on the
lab account.

- Specs: `assets/clm-workflows/specs/<id>.json`
- Compiler: `src/clm-workflow-spec.ts` (`validateClmSpec`, `compileClmWorkflow`)
- Shared Start-step variables: `assets/clm-workflows/base-variables.json`
- Output schema: `docs/schemas/clm-workflow.schema.json` (`check('clm-workflow', …)` in `src/asset-schemas.ts`)
- Offline test: `test/clm-workflow-spec.test.ts`
- Live proof: `npx tsx captures/clm-workflow-verify.ts assets/clm-workflows/specs/<id>.json … --cdp`
  (report in `assets/clm-workflows/verify/<id>.json`)
- Deploy and park: a solution manifest's `clmWorkflows`, with `deploy-scenario --solution` and `park-scenario`
  (section 8)

Sources are marked [help] (the official "Workflows in Docusign CLM" PDF, 2026-06-26, which is the
authority), [observed] (our own runs on the lab account, 2026-10-29 and 2026-10-30) or [internal CLM reference] (the CLM
workflow file and parameter reference). Where they disagree, this page says so and follows [help].

## 1. Which file to target

CLM has three ways to move a workflow design in or out. We measured all three on 2026-10-29 [observed].

| | Designer ▸ Export / Import JSON | Admin ▸ Workflows ▸ Configuration ▸ Download Workflow | Admin ▸ Deployment (.spackage) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Direction | Export **and** Import | Download only; there is no upload | Export; install only in another account |
| File | `<name>_ V<n>.json` | `<name>.txt` | `<name>.spackage` |
| Content | JointJS graph `{cells}` | The same `{cells}` graph. Only icon paths (`/atlassupport` vs `/clm/atlassupport`) and `isSecret` on variables differ | Zip of `Data.spackage` + `Thumbprint.xml` (a signature). `Data.spackage` is a zip of `Version.xml`, `Manifest.xml`, `FolderTree.xml` and `workflows/<acct>_<name>` (the same `{cells}` JSON) |
| Dependencies | None (references by GUID) | None | Not included |
| Round trip in one account | Yes | No | No: the origin account opens it as an editable package with no Install button |
| Endpoint | POST `/designer/importjson`, then POST `/designer/save` | GET `/clm/workflow/exportWorkflowVersionDefinition` → `{success, designDefinition: '<json string>'}` | `/clm/Packaging/EditPackage.aspx` |

**The compiler targets the designer's Import JSON.** It is the only path that goes both ways, and it is the
path the guide documents for cloning [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.12] and for moving a workflow from UAT to Production [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.204].

### How Import behaves [observed]

- Import **replaces the open canvas**, including the name, which it takes from `Start.workflowName`.
- Nothing is stored until **Save**. Saving into an existing workflow overwrites its draft and renames the
  definition. To make a new one: New Workflow ▸ Advanced Workflow ▸ "This workflow will start without
  content" ▸ Import ▸ set the name ▸ Save. The result is an Advanced Workflow; any template link is lost.
- A name that is already used is refused with HTTP 200 `{success: false, "A workflow with name … already exists."}`.
  A refused character in the name is also a 200 `success: false`. **Check the response, not the page.**
- A file that is not a workflow returns 200 `{definition: null}`, and the canvas silently resets to just Start.
- An unknown user GUID is accepted by Save **and** by Publish. Nothing checks it.
- Import does not publish. Publish is needed before the workflow can run [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.10] [internal CLM reference].
- Saving into a **published** version adds a revision to it (1.1 → 1.2), the version running instances use. To change
  a live workflow without touching its running instances: Versions and Publishing ▸ **Create New Version**
  (`POST /clm/workflow/designer/createVersion`), Import, Save, then that version's **Publish**. Instances started
  before keep their version (2026-11-20: Test 1/4/8 and Fontara, every Executing run stayed on 1.1).

### Canvas layout

The compiler places the steps (src/clm-workflow-layout.ts): left to right by longest path from Start, the main path on
one row (each step's nearest post-dominator), every other branch on its own row above or below, finish steps in the
last column. A shared end step that two or more steps lead to (e.g. one "rejected" handler) gets a row under the rest,
and a step only failure links lead to ("Log failure") sits on the bottom row under the last column; their links drop
down the gap beside each step (port `es` plus a link vertex), and loops back run between the rows (ports `n`/`s`).
The designer keeps link ports and `vertices` through Import, Save and Publish. Position, ports, vertices and step names
do not change what a workflow does: `designWithoutLayout` drops them, and test/clm-workflow-layout.test.ts holds every
spec's result to a fixture. To re-lay out a deployed workflow keeping its site settings: `relayoutDeployed(export, compiled)`.

### Promotion flow

The documented flow from a test account to Production [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.204] [internal CLM reference]:

1. In the source account, open the workflow and choose **Export ▸ Export JSON**.
2. In the target account, open the designer and choose **Import**; pick the JSON file.
3. Give the workflow a new name and **Save**.
4. Review what does not travel: user and group GUIDs, folder and document IDs, Salesforce and integration
   references, XPath expressions and document paths [internal CLM reference]. Update every **Maestro Workflow**
   step to the Workflow Builder workflow in the target account [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.204].
5. **Publish** and start a controlled test instance; check the output paths and any generated documents.

Workflow Builder workflows that a CLM workflow calls must be rebuilt in Production and must have unique
names; a Workflow Builder workflow without a unique name fails when it runs [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.204].

## 2. The spec format

```json
{
  "id": "external-review-with-comment-check",
  "name": "External Review Comment Check",
  "description": "Free text, not compiled.",
  "variables": ["Comments"],
  "steps": [
    { "id": "review", "kind": "externalReview", "assignee": "submitter", "subject": "Please review",
      "on": { "sent": "wait", "rejected": "outRejected", "canceled": "outRejected", "failure": "outRejected" } },
    { "id": "finish", "kind": "finish" }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `id` | File name and GUID seed. GUIDs are SHA-1 of `<id>/<step id>`, so the same spec always compiles to the same file. |
| `name` | Letters, digits, spaces, `-`, `_` and `'` only; at most 100 characters [observed]. The verify script prefixes `ZZ Lab - `. |
| `variables` | Extra **Text** variables. `Params` and `SubmittedBy` and the other built-ins come from `base-variables.json`. |
| `noContent` | `true`: the workflow starts without content (by hand, a schedule, or the API with no Params). Params gets an empty schema, and a step that reads Params or the incoming documents is refused. Lab: `clm-step-lab starts` (queued); a custom XML start (no documents) is `paramsSchema` with that XML. |
| `steps` | The first step follows Start. Each step has `id`, `kind`, optional `name` (the canvas label) and `description` (shown under the step). |
| `next` / `on` | `next` for a step with one path; `on` maps each outcome to a step id. An outcome left out has no link. |

A participant (`assignee`, `to`) is `"submitter"` (the `SubmittedBy` variable) or `{ "user": "<email>" }`; a task's `assignee` can also be a task group, `{ "taskGroup": "<name>", "member": <participant> }` (see "Task groups" below). On the lab account, `clm-workflow-verify --user-map=<spec email>=<account email>` resolves a spec's cast address to the account user (the only CLM user there); `named-approver-with-system-variables` was started that way with `--run` (its Approve step waited on that user).
An email is resolved to the account's CLM user GUID **at deploy** (the verify script and `deploy-scenario --solution`
ask the address book through `clmUserId` in `captures/lib-clm-workflow.ts`), because CLM does not check GUIDs itself.

### Step kinds

Each kind compiles to a cell copied from a real export, so only settings seen in an export are written.
A kind that no export has shown is refused, not guessed.

| `kind` | CLM step (activityName) | Fields | Outcomes in `on` → link label CLM writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `setVariable` | Update Variable Value (`UpdateVariableActivity`) | `set: {variable: value}`: text (merge tags allowed), or `{ "var": "<path>" }` for the value at a variable path as text (an expression, `return Convert.ToString(GetVariableValue("Params.Params.Documents…"));`), or `{ "map": "<Text variable>", "cases": { "<answer>": "<value>" } }`: the value for the answer held in that variable (a Routing step's output; each answer must be one of its options), else the variable keeps its value. The table is written into the step's description and as comments in the expression. Run-proven 2026-11-20 (Test 4: "Payment terms now Net 90" set the Number variable PayDays to 90 and left Verdict as it was) | `next` |
| `externalReview` | Review and Send for External Review (`ReviewAndSendForExternalReviewActivity`) | `assignee`, `subject`, `body` (the task assignment email), `instructions`, `rejectText`, `comments` (`Yes`/`No`/`Required`), `timeoutDays`, `toVar` (a Text variable: the task's To), `email: { subject, body }` (the external review email as the task opens; CLM requires both before Send), `displayName` | `sent` → `action Completed - External Review Sent by Sender`; `rejected` → `action Completed - External Review Rejected by Sender`; `canceled` → `action canceled`; `failure`; `timeout` (needs `timeoutDays`) → the timer's `referenceKey` GUID |

More shared task settings (harvest B): `businessDays` (the due date's calendar `Business Hour`; needs a due date) [observed, acceptance 8, Test 4: a Choice with `due: { days: 10 }` and `businessDays` was due 30 working days later: the calendar counts a Period day as 24 business hours, three 8-hour days, so write a third of the working days], `customAction: {label, url}` (a button that opens the URL in a new window), `cancellation: {by, to}` (Workflow Step Cancellation; `by` users may cancel too; `to` is the Step Cancelled path; not on a Choice), `compareWithPrevious` (compare the document with its previous version). A spec's `errorNotify` (Whos) turns on the Start step's "Send a notification when workflow encounters an error". With `"submitter"` the designer's panel shows Users To Receive Notification empty, though the export holds the SubmittedBy variable (Test 4, 2026-11-20). A step whose outcome has no link ends the run there: Workflow Activity lists it as **Failed** and the process monitor stops at that step (Test 4, 2026-11-20: Contract Request to Execution 3.1 started without a document failed at Mark In Review, 3 activities). The account's own Advanced Workflow Error Notification User (CLM Admin ▸ Account Settings ▸ Workflow & Tasks) is a separate, account-wide setting. Update Security is not offered on the lab CLM account and is not compiled; the start's content type (a folder start) is chosen in New Workflow and is not in the Import JSON.

**Rule conditions** (harvest 2026-11-02): a Rule's `condition` is one comparison or `{ all: [...] }` (and) / `{ any: [...] }` (or); each comparison is `{left, op, right}`. Rules and Decision branches take `op` `equals` (=), `notEquals` (<>), `contains`, `greaterThan` (>, stored `gt`), `greaterOrEqual` (>=, `gtoet`), `lessThan` (<, `lt` [inferred]) and `lessOrEqual` (<=, `ltoet` [inferred]). The designer also offers In, Not in, Contains data, Does not contains data, Not contains, and for a picked Text variable Begins with, Does not begin with, Ends with, Does not end with: not compiled (their stored codes are not harvested). Each comparison but the last carries the joiner, as the designer stores it.

**More variable types** (harvest): `idList` (ID List) and `iterator` (with `of`: `<xml var>.<repeating node path>`, e.g. a Document variable's `Renewals.Documents.Document` [the help: an iterator points at a node that repeats in an XML variable]; an iterator over an ID List imports, but the For-Each throws at run time [observed 2026-11-02, run 83a1648d], so the compiler refuses it); any typed variable takes `description` and `secret` ("Do not display variable value"). `setVariable` takes `{ code: "return …;" }` for a C# expression (the gear's Expression Builder).

**Canvas boxes**: `groups: [{ name, steps }]` and `pools: [{ name, lanes: [{ name, steps }] }]` draw a Group, or a Pool with Lanes, around those steps. The designer stores no parent or embeds, only position and size, so the boxes change nothing at run time. Run-proven 2026-11-02 ([lab](../assets/clm-workflows/verify/renewal-notice-batch-lab.json): run 29df1375).

The kinds above `finish` were written from one export each. The kinds below it compile from
`assets/clm-workflows/cell-templates.json`: one cell per activity, harvested read-only on 2026-10-29 from the
lab account's own workflows (their Export JSON) and cleaned (free text blanked, people and account variables
removed). The link labels come from the designer's own step catalogue, `GET /clm/workflow/designer/getDesignerPresentation`
(`activities.<name>.outputs`), which also lists every step's settings for all 109 palette items [observed].
No export had a Document Generation step, so its cell is built from that catalogue alone.
Choice and Find Document come from the account's Example Workflow and Document Version Workflow exports. No export had an
Edit Document step: its cell is the Approve cell without Approve's own settings (`checkoutDocuments`, `assignedUsersInOrder`,
`approveText`, `rejectText`, `requiredApprovalCount`), and every key left is one the catalogue lists for `EditDocumentsActivity`.
Find Document compiles only a variable source (Params or a declared variable), the only source the exports show; the
help's other sources (a CLM path, a text variable with a document id) are not compiled.

**Task groups.** Every task kind (`approve`, `choice`, `editDocument`, `createOrUploadDoc`, `reviewAndSendForSignature`,
`externalReview`) takes `"assignee": { "taskGroup": "<name>", "member": <who> }` (Assign to a task group). It compiles to
`assigneeType: "workerpool"`, `assignedWorkerPools` (`WorkerPool`: the group's `Guid`) and `assignedWorkerPoolUsers` (the
Task Group Assignee; empty without `member`, so the task is open to every member), with no `assignedUsers`: the shape of
the account's Example Workflow Choice and xVISUALx Approve [observed]. A group's uid is account-bound, like a folder's: the
account values' `clmTaskGroups` (name → uid) give it, and `clm-workflow-verify --task-groups=<name>=<uid>` on the lab;
without them the group compiles empty and the bundle README names the step to pick it in after Import. The group's
Auto-Assign Pattern (Random, Round Robin, Least Used Resource) is a setting of the task group (Admin ▸ Task Groups), not of
the step [help: cef1677277656287]. A group uid that the account does not have still imports, saves, publishes and opens
with no error state, but at run time the step fails: "Could not parse '0|<uid>' as worker pools", and the run follows the
step's Failure path [observed 2026-10-31, lab run with the uid from the account's Example Workflow; most likely that
template names a group the account does not have]. So take the uid from Admin ▸ Task Groups or the designer's picker on the target
account, never from another workflow. Picking a group in the designer (Assigned Task Group ▸ View Options ▸ Legal ▸
Apply ▸ Save) saves exactly the shape the compiler writes: `assigneeType` workerpool, `assignedWorkerPools` with the
group's `Guid`, `assignedWorkerPoolUsers` [observed 2026-10-31; the lab CLM account offers Finance, Legal, Procurement, Sales and
Specialists]. With that uid the lab run waited at the Choice, its task in the starter's Tasks
([lab report](../assets/clm-workflows/verify/contract-triage-task-group-lab.json): Find Document filled its variable). The
Choice task opens on the document page with a Tasks panel: the options are a required dropdown "Choose one of the
following", then a Message box and **Complete**. The lab picks the option with the dropdown (a native select) and
presses Complete; the Edit Document task has Complete only. Proven 2026-10-31 (run 3b9fb864): the Choice went to the
Legal task group, "Needs edits" led to the Edit Document task, and the run Completed, so Choice, Edit Document, Find
Document and the task-group assignee are proven live. [`contract-triage-task-group`](../assets/clm-workflows/specs/contract-triage-task-group.json)
uses all three new kinds and a task group; its lab is `npx tsx captures/clm-step-lab.ts tasks --task-group=<uid of a task group on the account>`.

**Shared task settings** (proven 2026-11-01 on Routing: every setting stored as compiled after the designer saved the import, and the task ran; [lab](../assets/clm-workflows/verify/matter-folder-and-routing-lab.json). Read a finished run's Text variables from the process monitor: `getvariablexml` answered empty for them). `approve`, `choice`,
`editDocument` and `routing` take, and `reviewAndSendForSignature` takes all but `respond`:

| Key | Designer setting | Compiles to |
|---|---|---|
| `respond: "any" \| "all"` | Who needs to respond? | `requiredCompletion` `{type: Number, value: 1}` (any, the default every export has) or `{type: Percentage, value: 100}` (all) [inferred: the catalogue's radio values, no export had "all"] |
| `from` | Task Assignment Email ▸ Email sender | `notificationFromAddress` (a participant, as the account's Contract - * Choice steps store `SubmittedBy`) |
| `reminders: [{ afterDays, everyHours?, to? }]` | Reminders ▸ ADD REMINDER (first, recurring) | `timers`: one timer per reminder, shaped like the due-date timers the exports store, output "Reminder <n>" with its `referenceKey`; `everyHours` as a recurring Period with `recurringChecked` [inferred]. `to` links the reminder path (a parallel thread; the task stays open) by that key |
| `commentsTo` | Output ▸ Store comments in a variable | `outputComments` (a Text variable) |
| `displayName`, `stage` | Display Name, Stage Name | `activityDisplayName` (default the step label), `stageName` (default the workflow name) |
| `linkToNext` | Link to next step | `waitForNextStep` true; refused unless the next step is a task of the same assignee |
| `due: { months, weeks, days }` | Due Date ▸ after the step is assigned | the `timeout` timer's Period (instead of `timeoutDays`; the timer has no hours or minutes field) |

Approve also takes `assignees` (several users instead of `assignee`) with `inOrder` (Assign tasks in order?, `assignedUsersInOrder`), and `checkout` (Checkout the document?, `checkoutDocuments`). Email and Email Document take `from` (a Who; default the starter). Wait for External Review takes `outputDocuments` and `updatedDocuments` (Document variables). A step name is at most 200 characters (the designer's maxlength) and a variable name at most 250 letters and digits [help: woi1737643109961]; the compiler refuses longer ones. Proven 2026-11-02 ([lab](../assets/clm-workflows/verify/contract-approval-chain-lab.json): run dcbc234c, settings stored, the approval's checkout and display name seen at run time).

"Make a new variable" or "Use an existing variable" in an Output box store the same thing (a variable reference); a new one
is a variable declared in `variables`.

**Variables.** `variables` takes a name (Text) or `{ "name", "type": "text" | "number" | "date" | "xml" | "document" | "folder" | "user", "schema" }`.
A `user` variable (Actor) gets SubmittedBy's UserAccount schema (Name, Email, Uid …), as the Contract - * exports declare Choose Users' output; proven 2026-11-01 (the review lab).
`schema` is a sample XML; the compiler turns it into the designer's schema tree (`nodes`: elements with children,
leaf elements and attributes, each with a GUID), so the XPath pickers and `<%#XmlVariables…%>` paths resolve.
`paramsSchema` does the same for the incoming `Params`. A step that names a variable must name a declared one,
and an XML input must be an XML, Document or Folder variable.

Text fields take merge tags such as `<%#Variable.EmailBody%>` and
`<%#XmlVariables.Params.Documents.Document.Name%>` (see ASSET-FORMATS, "CLM doc-gen and Gen for Salesforce Word templates").
The documents of review and email steps are always the incoming `Params` documents.

Every workflow should end at a **Finish** step: without one, a workflow that stops on a failure shows as
"Complete" in the activity monitor instead of "Failure", and a waiting parent workflow does not resume [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.104].

## 3. Variable model

The Start cell holds every variable (`definedVariables`). The guide's types [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.124]–[help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.127]:

| Type | Use |
|---|---|
| Params ("incoming content") | What started the workflow. **Do not change it**; copy it to another variable first [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.125] [internal CLM reference]. Empty when the workflow starts without content [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.9]. |
| Text | Plain text: rule comparisons, email merges, step inputs [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.126]. A spec variable given by name only is Text. |
| Number | An integer; usable in C# expressions [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.126]. |
| Date | A date, e.g. an effective date taken from Params [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.124]. |
| ID List | IDs of many documents or folders, e.g. a Find step's output [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.125]. |
| Iterator | Points to a node in another XML variable that occurs at least once; drives a For-Each Loop [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.125]. |
| XML types: Actor, Custom XML, Document, Folder | Structured data with a schema, which fills the variable pickers [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.127]. |

- **System variables**: `<%#System.Link%>` (task link for this instance), `<%#System.Date%>`,
  `<%#System.Time%>`, `<%#System.Uid%>` (the instance ID; put it in every failure email) [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.130]. Export the
  workflow as JSON to see the full list [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.130].
  [observed] They go into any text field of a spec as they are. [`named-approver-with-system-variables`](../assets/clm-workflows/specs/named-approver-with-system-variables.json)
  puts all four in its Approve and Email steps; it imported, published, started and cancelled clean on 2026-10-30.
- **Caret variables** (`^<step name><thing>`, e.g. `^Find Document 1DocumentIds`) are written by CLM when a
  step completes; they appear in the process monitor [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.131].
- **Redaction**: a variable with **Do not display variable value** shows "Redacted" in the process monitor.
  It does not redact values passed by Update Parent Variable or values inside a logged expression [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.16].
  In the export this is the variable's `isSecret` [observed].

## 4. Starting a workflow

- **By hand**: Admin ▸ Workflows ▸ Configuration ▸ check a **published** workflow ▸ Start Workflow. Optionally
  choose a document, or **Provide custom parameters** and paste the Params XML [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.11].
- **By API** [observed 2026-10-30]: `POST {ApiBaseUrl}/v2/{accountId}/workflows` with `{"Name": "<workflow name>",
  "Params": "<Params>…</Params>", "WorkflowDocuments": {"Items": [{"Href": "{ApiBaseUrl}/v2/{accountId}/documents/<uid>"}]}}`.
  `Name` is the definition's name and is the only required field; the workflow must be **published**. `Params` is an XML
  string; it must be well formed and contain every node the workflow's XPath reads (an empty string is accepted for a
  workflow that starts on documents). The answer is the run (`Status: Executing`, `Href` ending in its id);
  `GET …/workflows/{id}` reads it back and `DELETE …/workflows/{id}` stops it (`Aborted`). See "API start" below.

### API start [observed 2026-10-30]

The client is `src/clm-api.ts`. Two things are easy to get wrong:

- **The host.** CLM is spread over data centres and its API host is not in `/oauth/userinfo`. Ask the auth service:
  `GET https://authuat.springcm.com/api/v2/{apiAccountId}/account` (production: `auth.springcm.com`) answers
  `ApiBaseUrl` [help: developers.docusign.com/docs/clm-api/clm101]. For the lab account it is
  `https://api.s1.us.clm.demo.docusign.net` (web app `s1.us.clm-d.docusign.com`, the lab CLM account). A token sent to another
  data centre's host (`apiuatna11.springcm.com`) answers **401**, which looks like a missing scope and is not one.
- **The ids and the token.** The CLM API account id is the **eSignature API account GUID** (`00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` here), not the
  CLM `aid`. The token needs `spring_read` / `spring_write`. The eSignature web app's own bearer (what it sends to
  `/api/esign/…`) already carries them, so a lab script with the signed-in profile uses that; a headless caller (an ERP)
  uses a JWT grant for its own integration key with `signature impersonation spring_read spring_write`
  (`DS_CLM_*` in `.env`). `clmApi()` takes the JWT path when `DS_CLM_INTEGRATION_KEY` is set.
- **The key** (the lab account, 2026-10-30): Admin ▸ Apps and Keys ▸ Add App and Integration Key
  "Fontara Demo Gallery CLM" (`e318499c-…`), Private custom integration, our own RSA public key (Upload RSA; the private
  key is a local key file), redirect URI `http://localhost:8080/callback`. A new redirect URI took about two
  minutes to work ("There are no redirect URIs registered" until then). Consent once, signed in as the user:
  `clmConsentUrl()` ▸ Allow Access (the page lists only the eSignature scope's description; the spring scopes are
  granted anyway). Admin pages and the consent page ask for the password again even in a signed-in profile.

Smoke test (read-only): `npx tsx captures/clm-api-smoke.ts` (member + workflow definitions). Live proof:
`npx tsx captures/clm-workflow-verify.ts assets/clm-workflows/specs/internal-approval-and-signature.json --api`
publishes the ZZ Lab copy, uploads a ZZ document, starts the run by API, reads it back, stops it, and deletes both
(report `assets/clm-workflows/verify/internal-approval-and-signature-api.json`; ledger `captures/clm-workflow/ledger.json`).

- **Document Generation**: the Params schema (with `TemplateFieldData`) only appears after the configuration
  has started the workflow once. Design against a run of an empty workflow [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.21] [internal CLM reference].
  [observed] Our build does it in one pass: [`nda-request-launched`](../assets/clm-workflows/specs/nda-request-launched.json)
  declares the `TemplateFieldData` of the form [`nda-request-conditional`](../assets/clm-docgen-forms/specs/nda-request-conditional.json)
  in `paramsSchema`. `captures/clm-docgen-config-verify.ts` saved that form, its Word template and a configuration that
  launches the published workflow, generated once through the Doc Launcher form, and the launched run completed with the
  typed values in Params (2026-10-30, `assets/clm-docgen-forms/verify/nda-request-conditional.json`).
- **eForm** [observed 2026-10-30]: a classic eForm's Routing ▸ Set Workflow starts a run per submit, with the `.sxform` as
  the Params document: attributes at `Document/<Group>/<Field>` (spaces and punctuation dropped), custom inputs at
  `Document/CustomFormFields/<id>` (only letters and digits kept) and in `CustomFormData`. The process monitor shows Params;
  `GET …/workflows/{id}` does not. See [CLM workflows guide § 19](clm-workflows.html#guide-19-start-from-an-eform) and
  [CLM eForms](clm-eforms.html).
- **eForm answers in a run, end to end** [observed 2026-10-31, acceptance 4 and its fix run,
  [report](../assets/prompt-corpus/live/proc-clm-supplier-agreement-eform.json)]: an eForm submit started the corpus example
  `proc-clm-supplier-agreement-eform`. What holds:
  - read an answer into a Text variable with `setVariable` `{ "var": "Params.Documents.Document.CustomFormFields.<id>" }`. An
    Evaluate an XPath into a **Text** variable matched the node and then failed the step ("Action failed with exception");
  - merge tags in an Approve step's instructions show the answers in the task, which matters because an `.sxform` has no
    preview there;
  - Document Generation with `outputDocuments` needs `outputDocumentName` to publish; a merge tag in it names the file after
    the supplier, and Send for Signature with `documents: {var}` sends that file, not the `.sxform`;
  - a Doc Gen **Text Box** filled by the step's input XML prints as raw HTML (`<html><head>…<body>…`); a text field prints
    clean, but a line break in the answer is dropped;
  - a recipient `name` is the name on the envelope; without it the recipient is named by the email address;
  - the configuration's own "Launch a workflow" does not run when another workflow's Document Generation step uses the
    configuration; and a step that names the configuration by another name fails ("Failed to find Document Generation
    configuration").
- **eForm answers into a Doc Gen form** [observed 2026-10-31]: a `prefillXml` step turns the answers into the form's
  input XML, and a Create or Upload Doc step with that `inputXml` opens the form filled in
  ([`eform-request-prefills-draft`](../assets/clm-workflows/specs/eform-request-prefills-draft.json),
  `captures/clm-step-lab.ts prefill`, [report](../assets/clm-workflows/verify/eform-request-prefills-draft-lab.json)).
  The lab started the run by API with Params shaped like the `.sxform`. What it showed:
  - every field of the Contract Draft form held its answer: a dropdown, text, currency (`125000.00`), and dates
    (the ISO `2026-11-01` showed as `11/1/2026`);
  - a Text Box is rich text: the answer appears inside `<p>`, and an escaped `<ZZ>` in it was read as a tag and dropped;
  - the task opens `…/doclauncher/form/<configuration>?wfid=…`. A configuration that launches no workflow opens as
    "Invalid Document Generation configuration", for the task and for the plain launcher link alike, so the lab's
    configuration launches the lab workflow.

## 5. Limits that matter for a design

| Limit | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Activities per workflow instance | 10,000; over the limit the workflow is paused and given a purge date | [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.14] |
| Abort of Executing/Paused workflows | after 365 days (Production), 90 days (UAT) | [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.190] |
| Account purge schedule | 7–30 days after complete / after fail; default 7 | [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.191] |
| Start step purge fields | `daysTillPurgeOnSuccess` 0, `daysTillPurgeOnFailure` 30 in every export we saw | [observed] |
| Business-day due dates | a business day counts as 8 hours, Monday–Friday | [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.18] |
| Workflow name | letters, digits, spaces, `-`, `_`, `'`; at most 100 characters | [observed] |

Conflict: the Start step's success purge field (0) is below the account schedule's 7–30 range. They are
separate settings; we have not seen which one wins. Follow the account setting [help: CLM Workflows guide 2026-06-26, p.191].

## 6. Validation checklist

**Design time** — `validateClmSpec` refuses the spec when:

- the name has a refused character or is over 100 characters;
- two steps share an id, a kind is unknown, or a `next`/`on` target does not exist;
- a `setVariable` sets an undeclared variable;
- an `evaluateXPath` writes into a variable that is not XML (it fails at run time; read a value as text with `setVariable` `{ "var": "<path>" }`);
- a `documentGeneration` with `outputDocuments` has no `outputDocumentName`;
- an account value or a folder `uid` is made up (`src/made-up-id.ts`: all zeros, one character repeated in a group of 8 or 12, `12345678-…`, `placeholder…`); give a folder by `{name}` instead;
- a step other than Finish has no way out, a step cannot be reached from the first step, or there is no Finish;
- a `timeout` outcome has no `timeoutDays`, or a `{user}` participant has no GUID. In a solution bundle built without account values, such a participant compiles to an empty assignee instead, and the README names the step to pick it in after Import: an empty assignee imports, saves and even publishes [observed 2026-10-31], so nothing else forces the pick.

Also review by hand [internal CLM reference]: XPath against the real Params schema, matching variable types,
every output stored in a named variable, and failure paths that email `<%#System.Uid%>`.

**Deploy time** — `captures/clm-workflow-verify.ts` gates, per spec:

| Gate | Passes when |
|---|---|
| compile | the spec compiles and the output passes `clm-workflow.schema.json` |
| import | `/designer/importjson` returns a definition (not `null`) |
| save | `/designer/save` returns `success: true` and the name appears in the definition list |
| readBack | the Download Workflow export has every compiled step (activityName + name) and the same link labels |
| designer | the saved workflow opens with no step in an error state (screenshot) |
| publish (`--run` or `--publish`; `--publish` keeps the published copy for a lab that needs it, e.g. a doc-gen configuration's "Launch this workflow") | the designer's Versions panel ▸ Publish answers `success` and the definition shows `IsPublished` |
| start (`--run`) | POST `/clm/workflow/startWorkflow` (what Start Workflow sends: `versionUid`, `definitionUid`, `startWorkflowInfo: {DocumentUids, Params}`) starts a run on a fresh ZZ document and it appears in Activity |
| cancel (`--run`) | the process monitor's **Cancel this workflow** (no confirmation) leaves the run **Aborted** |
| start, readRun, cancel (`--api`) | as `--run`, through the CLM REST API (`src/clm-api.ts`): POST `/v2/{accountId}/workflows` {Name, Params, WorkflowDocuments}, GET the run (Executing), DELETE it (Aborted). Report `<id>-api.json` |
| cleanup | the `ZZ Lab -` copy is deleted, after checking its exact name and id; with `--run`, the ZZ document too (to Trash). Not with `--keep` or `--publish` |

Last runs: every library spec passed every gate it ran. On 2026-10-29: `msa-negotiation-external-review` (17 steps, 26 links),
`external-review-with-comment-check` (9, 15), `docgen-intake-and-child` (6, 12) and `internal-approval-and-signature`
(9, 20), the last with `--run`: published, started on a ZZ document, cancelled (Aborted), all deleted. On 2026-10-30:
`named-approver-with-system-variables` (5, 7) with `--run` and `--user-map` (the same run, cancel and cleanup), and
`nda-request-launched` (5, 6) with `--publish`, kept for the doc-gen configuration lab that launched it.

**Run time** [internal CLM reference]: publish, start a controlled instance, and check each outcome path, the
workflow output and any generated documents in the process monitor. Only `--run` starts a run, and it cancels that run; `--publish` publishes without a run.

## 7b. Renewals, vendor paper, CLM with IAM, renaming

Learned on enterprise CLM builds, 2026-11-20 to 11-23.

Smart rules and reminder templates are site configuration, not workflow files: the bundle README lists the ones a
workflow needs, and an admin makes them (Admin ▸ Smart Rules).

### Renewals

- **Start a renewal review from dates.** Reminder templates on a date attribute (Renewal review due = Expiration
  Date − 18 weeks, about 90 business days; Agreement expires in 30 days; Notice deadline in 30 days). Rule 1, on an
  executed contract whose Renewal Status is *Not due*: set *Scheduled* first (so the rule runs once), then schedule the
  reminders. Rule 2, on *Document Reminder Processed* with Renewal Status = *Scheduled*: start the review, which sets
  *Under review*, so the later reminders start nothing.
- **A failing rule action stops the later ones.** A contract without automatic renewal has no Termination Notice
  Date, so put the notice reminder last.
- **No reminder can be dated in the past**: a contract already inside its window needs its review started directly
  (Renewal Status *Review due*).
- **From Agreement Manager's obligations (CLM with IAM)**: the *Document Obligation Extracted* event starts a workflow
  that reads them with `useObligationData`. On demo CLM sites the step never finished, so keep that rule Disabled and
  keep the date reminders. The AI finds a renewal notice only when the contract states one (*CLM with IAM* below).

### Vendor paper, procurement and external review

- **Vendor paper (buy side)**: a rule on *Document Entered Folder* (`/Intake/Vendor paper`) starts the review. Keep
  the intake folder outside the executed-contracts tree, and the redline compares in a sibling folder, so the rule
  never sees its own output.
- **Review Data**: the person corrects what Use Docusign AI staged. Agreement Type is required: until it is set,
  every later task refuses Complete.
- **External review**: `externalReview` fills To (`toVar`), the email (`email: {subject, body}`) and the task's
  name (`displayName`); then `waitExternalReview` waits for the counterparty. The returned file is a new version: `compareDocumentVersions`
  keeps the compare for the last internal review (accept, another round, escalate).

### CLM with IAM (a CLM site integrated with Agreement Manager)

What carries to Agreement Manager, and what does not (lab, 2026-11-06 to 11-22):

- **Every new file in CLM becomes an Agreement Manager row**, agreement or not: templates, packages, eForms,
  certificates. Build templates and packages on a sandbox site and promote them by package.
- A document in a running CLM workflow is an *In progress* row; it turns *Completed* when the completion attribute
  (for example Contract Process ▸ Status = Executed) is set, within about a minute. Edits in Agreement Manager do not
  sync back to CLM.
- **Mapping** (Admin ▸ the Mapping Tool): nothing maps by name, except CLM Agreement Details' Effective Date, Expiration
  Date and Value. Mappable: String (no validation regex), Drop Down (map each option), Decimal, Date. Not mappable:
  Auto Number, Users and Groups, Dynamic Drop Down, sets. Create the Agreement Manager custom fields, linked to the
  agreement types, before you map, or the values land outside Details. **A mapped value replaces the AI's and stays**,
  through remaps and reprocessing: decide the mapping before the first documents arrive.
- **Value arrives as USD**, whatever the document's currency, over the AI's GBP or EUR amount. Write CLM Value only
  on USD agreements, and keep the currency in its own attribute.
- **Obligations are Agreement Manager's.** The AI finds only five kinds: one-time payment, deposit payment, renewal
  notice, termination for cause notice, termination for convenience notice. A contract states them that way
  ("a one-time fee of USD 4,500 due on 1 March 2027", "either party may terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice")
  or they are created by hand. CLM's own party-management obligations do not reach Agreement Manager.
- **Parent links do not carry**: CLM's agreement hierarchy (Document Review ▸ Hierarchy) makes no Agreement Manager
  hierarchy. Show families in CLM, or build them in Agreement Manager.
- **Deleting**: deleting a CLM-sourced row in Agreement Manager moves the CLM document to the CLM Trash. A document
  trashed in CLM leaves Agreement Manager's own list, but the public agreements list and the count keep it until
  it is **purged from the CLM Trash** (the public DELETE answered 204 and changed nothing).
- **Document Processed for AI Insights loops** with a workflow that runs Use AI Data Insights (the step reprocesses
  the document, so the event fires again: about 1,000 runs in 33 minutes, then CLM refused workflow starts for 45
  minutes). Start once per document from *Document Entered Folder*, set a marker and run a Chained rule that starts
  the workflow; the workflow checks the marker first. Before you enable a rule that starts a workflow, ask whether the
  workflow can raise the rule's event again.

### Renaming

- **A smart rule starts a workflow by its name.** Renaming the workflow makes the rule's Start Workflow action
  *Invalid*, and CLM refuses to save a rule with an Invalid action: re-point the action to the new name and save the
  rule in the same edit, keeping its Enabled or Disabled status.
- A `childWorkflow` step also calls its child by name: publish the parents again after a child is renamed.
- A run keeps the workflow name and version it started with; a step that looks for "the review's runs" by the new name
  misses them.
- Reminder templates, reports and dashboards are renamed one by one. A renamed attribute field keeps its CLM to
  Agreement Manager mapping.
- A just-saved rule can refuse Enable for about a minute.
- Name from the start without the company (`/Contracts`, `Legal Entity`, *Renewal review*): it saves all of this.

## 8. Deploy and park

A solution manifest (`docs/SOLUTION-SPEC.md`) lists CLM workflows in `clmWorkflows`. `captures/deploy-scenario.ts --solution`
deploys them on the CLM host before the doc-gen forms and configurations [observed, 2026-10-30]:

- **Import.** Each spec is compiled and imported as a new Advanced Workflow (New Workflow ▸ Advanced ▸ Import ▸ Save,
  `importClmWorkflow` in `captures/lib-clm-workflow.ts`, the path `clm-workflow-verify` proves). The name is
  `CLM_PREFIX` + the spec's name (`ZZ Lab - <name>` with `DEPLOY_LAB=1`; CLM names refuse `·`).
  `{ "user": "<email>" }` participants are resolved to CLM user GUIDs first.
- **Publish.** A workflow is published when a `clmDocgenConfigs` entry launches it (its `launch` may name a `clmWorkflows` id),
  and every one is published with `--publish`.
- **Ledger.** Each workflow is ledgered as `clm-workflows`; `--dry` lists the CLM workflows, forms, template documents
  and configurations it would make.
- **Own specs.** A manifest with its own specs (a corpus bundle's `<kind>/specs/` beside the manifest, or inline specs)
  deploys only as a lab: `DEPLOY_LAB=1`, "ZZ Lab" names. Under the demo names the deploy takes library specs only.

`captures/park-scenario.ts --scenario=<manifest id>` deletes them again, last and on the CLM host, by exact ledgered id
and name: doc-gen configurations, then CLM workflows, then forms and template documents. An id already gone is reported
and skipped. Live check (2026-10-30, lab): a manifest with one workflow, one form and a configuration launching the
workflow deployed; the Doc Launcher generated and the launched run completed; park deleted all four objects, and a
second park found them gone.

## Clause libraries (`assets/clm-clause-libraries`)

Not a workflow, but the CLM content workflows and doc-gen forms use: a clause library is one `.sxterm` document per clause,
and the file is a JSON array of the clause's options `{Name, Content, Notes, Uid, TermDocumentUid, StringId, IsModified}`
(what File ▸ Download gives; File ▸ Upload of it makes the library, Test 1 CLM 2026-11-10). `src/clm-clause-library.ts`
compiles a spec `{ id, name, folder, clauses: [{ name, options: [{ name, text, notes }] }] }` to those files (a term name
≤100 characters with `.sxterm`, notes ≤5000, no character CLM refuses in a name).
`captures/clm-clause-library-verify.ts <spec> --cdp --aid=<aid> --account="<CLM account>" --folder=<uid>` uploads each as
`ZZ Lab · <clause>.sxterm`, reads it back in the Terms editor and deletes it; `--deploy` loads the real names and keeps them.
A doc-gen form's Term field lists a library's options (row clm-form.field.term-sxterm).

## Parties (`assets/clm-parties`)

`src/clm-parties.ts` writes the CSV of CLM Admin ▸ Party Management ▸ Parties ▸ Actions ▸ Upload Parties List, with the
header of its own template (`PartyId,PartyName,ExternalId,BusinessContactName,PartyType,BusinessPhoneNumber,ShouldDelete`)
and the formatting help's name rules; the same rows with each PartyId and `ShouldDelete` true are the teardown.
Proven on Test 1 CLM 2026-11-10 by uploading the compiled CSVs by hand (create, then the ShouldDelete teardown); no verifier script yet (row clm-account.seed.parties-csv).

## Data files, Dynamic Drop Downs and CSV row choosers (`assets/clm-data-files`)

A CLM site keeps business lists as CSV documents in a folder, here `/_Custom_/System Files` (the layout of a legacy demo
site, 2026-11-24). `src/clm-data-file.ts` takes two shapes:

- a **list** `{ id, name, folder, values }`: one value a line, no header. A **Dynamic Drop Down** attribute reads it: in
  an attribute group spec (`src/clm-admin-spec.ts`) a field `{ name, type: "Dynamic Drop Down", source: "<list id>" }`
  compiles to type code 5 with `file|<folder>/<name>` in the form's values box. CLM reads the file as text each time the
  field shows, so a value has no comma or quote; a missing file makes the field's only value `Unable to load "file|…"`.
  The public API answers the field as `DynamicDropDown` with the file's values.
- a **table** `{ id, name, folder, columns, rows }`: a header row, then one row a record. A doc-gen form's CSV row chooser
  (`csvDropdown`, `csv: "<name>"`) reads it: the user picks a row by its `show` column and every linked field fills from
  its column. Above 10 KB the chooser is a type-ahead; up to 25 MB; a new version of the file updates the list.

Library: `counterparties` (28 invented portfolio counterparties, 19 columns: legal name, address, contact, customer number,
currency, payment terms), `internal-entities` (the company's 3 signing entities with signatory), and the lists `regions`,
`industries`, `party-types` for the attribute group `counterparty-profile`. The doc-gen form `order-form-from-party-list` is
the Platform Order Form with its parties picked: two choosers fill 22 fields, with the same merge tags, so it launches the
same *Generated Order Approval*.

Tools (each checks the CLM root folder name before writing; `--lab` uses ZZ Lab names and deletes what it made):

| Step | Tool | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| CSVs | `captures/clm-data-file-deploy.ts --cdp --aid= --account-id= --account= <id> …` | uploaded or a new version (REST upload host; a version needs `Content-Disposition` with a filename), read back byte for byte |
| Attribute group | `captures/clm-attribute-group-deploy.ts <spec> --cdp --aid= --account-id= --account=` | creates the group, or adds the fields an existing group lacks; checks each list is on the site first; reads the form and the public API back |
| Doc-gen form | `captures/clm-docgen-deploy.ts … --data="/_Custom_/System Files"` | a chooser's CSV uid is the document of that name in `--data` |
| The pick fills | `captures/clm-docgen-fill-verify.ts <spec> --cdp --aid= --account= --folder-path=` | opens the Doc Launcher, picks the spec's `sample` rows, every linked field shows its column's value; never presses Next |

## Custom actions (`assets/clm-custom-actions`)

A custom action is a menu entry: `{ id, name, where, does, openIn, passUser, passSelection, icon }`
(`src/clm-custom-action.ts`). `where`: `actionsMenu` (the header's Actions menu, on every page), `documentActions`
(Document Management ▸ Custom Actions, the "My Links" submenu), `fileItFolder`, `clmFiles` (CLM Files in Salesforce).
`does`: `{ docGen: "<configuration>" }` (`DocLauncher|<uid>`), `{ workflow: "<workflow>" }` (`Workflow|<uid>`; the run
gets the selected document as `Params/Documents/Document`) or `{ url }`. Names resolve to uids on the site at deploy.

There is no public API. `captures/clm-custom-action-deploy.ts --cdp --aid= --account= <id> … [--lab [--try-in=<folder>] | --delete]`
uses the Navigation & Actions page's own calls: `MenuActions/SaveAction` saves the entry and puts it on its menu
**disabled**; the menu is then saved back whole with that entry enabled (`SaveToolbar`), every other entry as it was;
`GetCustomAction` reads it back; `DeleteAction` removes it. For an Actions-menu doc-gen entry it clicks the entry and
expects the Doc Launcher. `--try-in` runs a workflow entry on a ZZ Lab document through CLM's action call
(`POST /clm/action?name=CustomMenuItem|<uid>`, the document as the Selection) and expects its run.

Where entries show (Test 4, 2026-11-24): Actions-menu entries in the header on every page. **My Links did not show** in
Document Review (the default document viewer since July 2025), the new search's row actions or the classic folder row
menu, also after a fresh sign-in, so a document workflow action works when called but a presenter cannot click it there.
A header entry that starts a workflow does not pass the document on screen: its run fails without one.
